items.followUp: Briefly describe the career of agriculture.

rubric.why: Identifies the main work of horticulture.
rubric.description: States that horticulture involves growing plants such as fruits, vegetables, or ornamental plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cultivation or management of these plants.

rubric.why: Describes a career or workplace in the field.
rubric.description: Gives an example of horticultural work or a place where horticulturists work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant role or workplace.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the science and career concerned with growing and managing fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants.
Horticulturists may work in nurseries, gardens, parks, or landscaping.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of a good scientific experiment.

rubric.why: A hypothesis must be capable of being tested.
rubric.description: States that a good hypothesis is testable.

rubric.why: A good hypothesis should be clearly expressed and grounded in observations or a prediction.
rubric.description: Gives another valid characteristic of a good hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant characteristic apart from testability.

modelAnswer: A good hypothesis is clearly stated and based on observations.
It must be testable by observation or experiment.

items.followUp: Define species and give its position in the taxonomic hierarchy.

rubric.why: A taxon is a unit or group used in classification.
rubric.description: Defines a taxon as a group or unit in biological classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition of taxon.

rubric.why: Taxonomic hierarchy arranges taxa in ranked levels.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomic hierarchy as the ordered arrangement of taxonomic groups or levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the ordered hierarchy.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a group or unit of organisms at any level of biological classification.
Taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of taxa in successive levels, such as species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, and kingdom.

items.followUp: Name two international organizations that work to conserve biodiversity.

rubric.why: WWF-Pakistan is one organization working for biodiversity protection in Pakistan.
rubric.description: Names WWF or its full name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for WWF-Pakistan or World Wide Fund for Nature.

accept: international union for conservation of nature
rubric.why: IUCN Pakistan is another organization working for biodiversity protection in Pakistan.
rubric.description: Names IUCN or its full name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for IUCN Pakistan or the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

modelAnswer: IUCN Pakistan (International Union for Conservation of Nature).

rubric.why: Filtration separates insoluble solid particles from a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the separation of insoluble solids from a liquid.

rubric.why: Filtration works by passing a mixture through a porous barrier.
rubric.description: Mentions passage through a filter or porous material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the filter or passage-through method.

modelAnswer: Filtration is the process of separating insoluble solid particles from a liquid by passing the mixture through a filter or other porous material.

rubric.why: Exocytosis moves substances out of the cell using vesicles.
rubric.description: Describes the outward movement and release of substances by exocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction and vesicle-mediated release.

rubric.why: Endocytosis brings substances into the cell by inward folding of the membrane.
rubric.description: Describes the inward movement of substances by endocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction and membrane or vesicle process.

modelAnswer: In exocytosis, vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane and release substances outside the cell.
In endocytosis, the plasma membrane folds inward to enclose substances in vesicles and bring them into the cell.

items.followUp: What is a centromere, and what is its role during cell division?

rubric.why: The kinetochore is a protein structure associated with a chromosome's centromere.
rubric.description: Identifies the kinetochore as a protein structure or complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its structure and location at the centromere.

rubric.why: The kinetochore provides the attachment site for spindle fibres during cell division.
rubric.description: States the kinetochore's role in spindle-fibre attachment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its attachment function during cell division.

modelAnswer: A kinetochore is a protein structure formed at the centromere of a chromosome.
It is the attachment site for spindle fibres during cell division.

rubric.why: Crossing over involves an exchange between chromatids.
rubric.description: States that crossing over is an exchange of chromosome segments or genetic material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the exchange.

rubric.why: The exchange occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis.
rubric.description: Identifies the chromatids or chromosomes involved and the stage of meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct participants or timing.

modelAnswer: Crossing over is the exchange of corresponding segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis.
